assumptions.choice: Interpreted 'MACD histogram rises for the last 3 bars' as 3 consecutive increases across 4 points: histo[-3] < histo[-2] < histo[-1] < histo[0]
assumptions.reason: spec wording is ambiguous about exact bar count; this is the most literal reading of 'rises for 3 bars'

assumptions.choice: Cross of MACD histogram above 0 implemented as previous bar histo <= 0 and current bar histo > 0
assumptions.reason: spec states 'crosses 0 from below' without an exact tie-breaking rule; treating the prior value as <=0 is the standard convention

assumptions.choice: Reused the BollingerBands(20,2) middle band (self.bb.lines.mid) as SMA(20) of Close for the fail-safe exit condition instead of instantiating a duplicate SMA(20) indicator
assumptions.reason: the Bollinger middle band is by definition SMA(period) of Close, numerically identical to the SMA(20) referenced only in the fail-safe rule; avoids a redundant indicator

assumptions.choice: The pending breakout stop order is cancelled and resubmitted every bar (while flat) using freshly computed base_high/base_low/ATR whenever all entry conditions still hold, and cancelled outright once any condition fails
assumptions.reason: a plain backtrader stop order cannot re-validate trend/consolidation/higher-low/momentum/volume after submission, so it must be actively re-armed each bar to track the current base and setup validity

assumptions.choice: Momentum (condition 4) and volume (condition 5) are evaluated on the same bar the stop order is (re-)armed, i.e. the signal/setup bar, rather than re-validated again on the future bar where the stop order actually fills
assumptions.reason: condition 5 explicitly says 'Volume today', anchoring these checks to the day the setup is confirmed; backtrader stop orders have no mechanism to re-check extra conditions only at fill time without cheat-on-open style order interception

assumptions.choice: base_high, base_low, base_height and ATR used for the initial stop-loss, TP1 and TP2 are frozen from the bar the entry order was last armed (not recomputed on the fill bar)
assumptions.reason: recomputing the 20-bar high/low after the breakout has already started would distort the base levels with post-breakout price action

assumptions.choice: Final size = floor(min(risk-based size, exposure-based size)) to an integer number of shares; if the resulting size is 0, no entry order is placed that bar
assumptions.reason: spec is silent on fractional shares and on the minimum-size edge case; backtrader default sizing is in whole units

assumptions.choice: TP1 closes floor(entry_size/2) shares and TP2 closes the remainder (entry_size - floor(entry_size/2))
assumptions.reason: spec says 'close 50% of the position' but shares must be whole numbers

assumptions.choice: '30 trading days' after entry implemented as 30 bars elapsed since the entry (breakout) bar, i.e. len(self) - entry_bar >= 30
assumptions.reason: each bar in this daily feed is one trading day, so bar count is the direct literal mapping

assumptions.choice: When a position is open, the fail-safe exit is checked before the time exit within the same bar; only one exit path executes per bar
assumptions.reason: spec lists both exits independently without specifying priority; checking fail-safe first is a reasonable default since it reacts to adverse price/momentum action

assumptions.choice: On TP1 fill, the existing full-size stop-loss order is cancelled and replaced with a new stop order at base_high (frozen from the armed base) sized to the remaining position
assumptions.reason: spec states 'move SL up to base_high' after TP1, which requires resizing since half the position has been closed
